There is delay of 1322 days in filing the instant appeal.
Though learned senior counsel for the respondents would vehemently contend that since there is such an inordinate delay, the appeal is not liable to the entertained,

Apart from perusing the reasons stated in the application seeking condonation of delay, what is also to be taken note in the instant case is that Civil Writ Petition No.
17896/2008 filed before the High Court of Punjab and Haryana at Chandigarh is with the challenge essentially to the Notifications issued under sections 4 and 6 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 by the appellants.

The appellants are assailing the order dated 27.10.2016, whereby the High Court only on the ground that the compensation was not deposited and the possession has not been taken, has allowed the Haryana State Industrial And ... vs Pyare Lal on 7 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26380119/
1 petition and has held that the acquisition has lapsed under Section 24(2) of the Act.

sentences.text: As already noticed above, the said position has been clarified in the cited decision and the compensation, if deposited, would be sufficient to indicate that the acquisition process is valid.
In the additional affidavit filed before the High Court, it is pointed out that a sum of Rs.45,37,65,530/- had already been deposited before the Land Acquisition Collector, Sonepat.
If this is the position, that aspect of the matter was required to be taken note by the High Court and thereafter an appropriate C.A. NO. 4944 OF 2023 consideration was required to be made.

If on the aspect relating to lapse of the acquisition as contemplated under Section 24(2) of the Act is not made out, in any event, the High Court will have to take into consideration the other aspects of the matter which has been raised in the writ petition.

Therefore, we deem it appropriate to set aside the order dated 27.10.2016 passed by the High Court of Punjab and Haryana at Chandigarh and restore the Civil Writ Petition No.17896 of 2008 to the Board of the High Court for consideration of the same, in accordance with law after providing opportunity to the parties.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Apart from perusing the reasons stated in the application seeking condonation of delay, what is also to be taken note in the instant case is that Civil Writ Petition No.
17896/2008 filed before the High Court of Punjab and Haryana at Chandigarh is with the challenge essentially to the Notifications issued under sections 4 and 6 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 by the appellants.
In that background, a perusal of the impugned order would disclose that the reason for which the writ petition has been allowed and was held that the acquisition has lapsed is in view of Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short `Act) based on the law that prevailed at that point of time.
Subsequently, a Constitution Bench of this Court has considered this aspect of the matter in the case of Indore Development Authority Vs. Manohar Lal & Ors. reported in (2020) 8 SCC 129.
In that view of the matter, taking note of all these aspects, we are of the opinion that the delay is liable to be condoned and the appeal is taken up for consideration.
If this is the position, that aspect of the matter was required to be taken note by the High Court and thereafter an appropriate C.A. NO. 4944 OF 2023 consideration was required to be made.
If on the aspect relating to lapse of the acquisition as contemplated under Section 24(2) of the Act is not made out, in any event, the High Court will have to take into consideration the other aspects of the matter which has been raised in the writ petition.

All contentions as urged in the writ petition, are left open to be urged therein and the consideration presently made shall not come in the way of the High Court in considering the matter in its entirety.
